ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, small ball A is placed on a smooth semicylindrical body fixed on a horizontal plane, and small ball B is pulled by a horizontal light spring and tied to a vertical plate. The two small balls A and B are connected by a light thin string through a smooth pulley O, and both balls are in a stationary state. It is known that the mass of ball B is m, point O is directly above the center $O_{1}$ of the semicylindrical body, OA makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction, the length of OA is equal to the radius of the semicylindrical body, and OB makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction. Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The mass of ball A is $\sqrt{6}m$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a smooth semicylindrical body fixed on a horizontal plane, with its center marked as O1, and directly above it there is a smooth pulley O. Small ball A is located on the upper-left surface of the semicylindrical body and is connected to the pulley through a thin string along the AO direction; small ball B is located on the right side and is connected to the pulley through the same thin string along the BO direction, while the right side of B is connected to a horizontal light spring, and the spring is fixed on a vertical plate. The dashed line in the figure indicates that O and O1 are on the same vertical line, and both A and B are stationary. Reasoning: Let the tension in the string be T, and the mass of ball A be M. Analyze the forces on ball B: B is acted on by gravity mg, string tension T, and the horizontal spring force. Since the spring force is horizontal, in the vertical direction only gravity and the vertical component of the tension balance. It is known that OB makes an angle of 45° with the vertical direction, so T cos45° = mg, giving T = √2 mg. Next analyze ball A. A is on the smooth semicylindrical surface and is acted on by gravity Mg, string tension T, and the supporting force N exerted on it by the semicylindrical body. It is known that OA is equal to the radius R of the semicylindrical body, and since A is on the cylindrical surface, O1A = R; also O is directly above O1, and OA makes an angle of 30° with the vertical direction, so in triangle OAO1, OA = O1A, from which it can be inferred that O1A also makes an angle of 30° with the vertical direction and is on the other side of the vertical line. Therefore, the tension T on A is along the AO direction, and the supporting force N is along the O1A direction; both make an angle of 30° with the vertical direction, and their horizontal components are in opposite directions. Horizontal equilibrium: T sin30° = N sin30°, so N = T. Vertical equilibrium: T cos30° + N cos30° = Mg. Substituting N = T gives 2T cos30° = Mg. Then substituting T = √2 mg gives M = 2√2 m cos30° = 2√2 m · √3/2 = √6 m.
